topic: Template Function with SFINAE for Type Constraints
explanation: In modern C++, template functions enable generic programming by allowing functions to operate on different data types. SFINAE (Substitution Failure Is Not An Error) is a technique used to conditionally enable or disable template functions based on properties of the template parameters, such as type traits. This allows for more precise control over template instantiation, ensuring that only suitable types invoke specific functions, which enhances type safety and code flexibility.
keywords: SFINAE, C++ type constraints, conditional template instantiation
